analysis.investment_thesis: KRN Heat Exchanger is a decent-quality business (ROCE ~20.8%) in a structurally growing HVAC/R sector, but at an EV/EBIT of ~113x the earnings yield is a catastrophic ~0.88% — the Magic Formula demands BOTH high ROIC and high earnings yield, and this stock fails the latter completely. No margin of safety exists at these prices regardless of growth rates.
key_strengths: Strong revenue CAGR of 40.2% (2022-2025) with operating profit growing even faster at 63.1%, showing operating leverage
Debt nearly eliminated (D/E: 0.06, debt dropped from INR 87 Cr to 33 Cr in one year) despite aggressive expansion
High promoter holding (70.79%) and global customer base across Asia, Europe, and Americas signals credible business model
key_risks: Earnings yield ~0.88% (EBIT INR 70 Cr / EV ~INR 7,916 Cr) — among the worst in the Magic Formula universe; any growth disappointment destroys the thesis
Free cash flow deeply negative (-INR 65 Cr in 2025) despite INR 53 Cr net profit, as capex of INR 151 Cr dwarfs operating cash flow of INR 21 Cr
P/E of 116x and EV/EBITDA of 85.7x price in decades of perfect execution — mean reversion in multiples alone could cause 60-70% drawdown
red_flags: Earnings yield of ~0.88% is 13x below Greenblatt's minimum attractive threshold of 12%
OCF/Net Profit conversion is only 40% (INR 21 Cr OCF vs INR 53 Cr profit) — profits are not translating to cash
INR 279 Cr investing outflows in 2025 (up from INR 64 Cr in 2024) — massive capital deployment that requires flawless execution to justify current valuation
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Using the Magic Formula: EBIT = INR 70 Cr, Enterprise Value = Market Cap (INR 7,893 Cr) + Debt (INR 33 Cr) – Cash (INR 10 Cr) = ~INR 7,916 Cr. Earnings Yield = 70/7,916 = **0.88%** — this is essentially zero by any value-investing standard. ROCE of 20.8% clears Greenblatt's quality bar (>20%), but Magic Formula requires BOTH cheap AND good. With one metric excellent and the other near-zero, this ranks in the bottom decile of any screener I'd run.

The business is real and growing impressively, but the market has already priced in many years of hypergrowth. Even if KRN sustains 40% revenue CAGR for 5 more years (an extraordinary assumption for a manufacturing company), the forward earnings would still struggle to justify today's price without multiple expansion remaining. Capex intensity is alarming: INR 151 Cr spent in 2025 against INR 53 Cr of profit, generating negative FCF of INR 65 Cr. A good business burning cash at this rate while trading at 116x earnings is a speculation, not an investment.
